rail_guard.text: Lincoln Central. The trains cross the High Street right in the middle of town, so half of Lincoln spends its life waiting at the barriers.
All aboard! Trains run to any station you've been to.

imp_spot.text: Up on the wall of Minster Yard a little stone figure sits cross-legged, grinning, with sausage grease on its chin.

then.text: The Lincoln Imp is yours. Best tell the Verger before he calls the police.

else.text: The Imp cackles and skitters off along the wall. He'll be back, he always is.

lin_yellowbelly.text: Ey up, me duck! Born and bred in Lincolnshire, which makes me a Yellowbelly. Nobody agrees why. Some say the yellow waistcoats of the old county regiment, some say the frogs in the fens.
Either way, it's a compliment. Mostly.

lin_cyclist_fan.text: Steep Hill, they call it. Sounds like a description, not a name, doesn't it? That's because it's a warning.
Halfway up there's a shop selling tea. That is not a coincidence.

lin_swans.text: The Brayford's a proper harbour, right in the middle of the city. The Romans brought boats up the Fossdyke from the Trent, and I bring mine up it now. Same water, more swans.
Mind the swans. They know they own the place.

lin_spire_guide.text: Over 55,000 aircrew of Bomber Command were killed in the war, more than four in every ten who flew. Their average age was about twenty-two.
Every name is on the walls. Families come and find theirs, and touch the letters.
